bull.b: TTM revenue rebounded sharply and gross margin improved, showing stronger commercial performance and better unit economics. If maintained, this recovery can support operating leverage and improve the company’s ability to fund growth without relying as heavily on external capital.

Positive TTM operating cash flow and slightly positive free cash flow mark a clear improvement from prior heavy cash burn. This gives the business a more viable internal funding base, although the small surplus still needs to become consistent before it offers substantial resilience.

Q2’s stronger gross profit and modest operating profit, together with higher cash, inventories, and equity, indicate that the recent recovery is reaching the operating business and balance sheet. If sustained, this can improve capacity to support expansion and ongoing capital needs.

bear.b: Despite revenue and gross-margin recovery, TTM net margin remained negative and EBITDA margin was only modestly positive. This leaves little room for execution errors or cyclical weakness, while sustained losses could constrain reinvestment and weaken financial flexibility.

Debt slightly exceeds equity and leverage remains elevated despite improvement from 2025. This raises financial risk, limits capacity to absorb a downturn, and can restrict funding for expansion while the company’s profitability recovery remains fragile and inconsistent.

bear.t: Thin and Inconsistent Free Cash Flow
bear.b: Although cash flow turned slightly positive, the very small free-cash-flow surplus provides limited protection if margins soften or working capital reverses. The sharp deterioration versus the prior annual period also shows that cash generation has not yet become dependable.
